Dear Sir or Madam:

By letter dated March 25, 2026 (Agencywide Documents Access and Management System
Accession No. ML26084A468), Holtec Palisades, LLC, (Holtec Palisades), submitted a Seismic
Probabilistic Risk Assessment report in response to Near-Term Task Force Recommendation
2.1, “Seismic,” for evaluation by the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC).

The NRC staff has identified the need for a regulatory audit to examine the licensee’s non-
docketed information with the intent to gain understanding, to verify information, or to identify
information that will require docketing to support the basis of the licensing or regulatory
decision.

The audit will be conducted using an online portal and teleconferences. Formal audit meetings
using video and teleconferencing will be scheduled as needed. The audit plan and supporting
materials are enclosed.

If you have any questions, please contact me at 301-415-2048 or via email at
Justin.Poole@nrc.gov.

                                    REGULATORY AUDIT PLAN

         REVIEW OF SEISMIC PROBABILISTIC RISK ASSESSMENT TO SUPPORT

                      THE NTTF 2.1 SEISMIC HAZARD REEVALUATIONS

                                    HOLTEC PALISADES, LLC

                                       DOCKET NO. 50-255


1.0   BACKGROUND

By letter dated March 25, 2026 (Agencywide Documents Access and Management System
Accession No. ML26084A468), Holtec Palisades, LLC, submitted a Seismic Probabilistic Risk
Assessment (SPRA) report in response to Near-Term Task Force (NTTF) Recommendation 2.1,
“Seismic,” for evaluation by the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC).

The NRC staff has initiated its review of the SPRA report and has determined that a regulatory
audit of the information identified in the Information Requests section below would assist in the
timely completion of the review process. The audit will be conducted in accordance with Nuclear
Reactor Regulation (NRR) Office Instruction NRR LIC-111, Revision 2, “Regulatory Audits”
(ML24309A281). The NRC staff continues to review other aspects of the licensee’s submittal
and may identify the need for additional audit subjects by separate correspondence.

2.0    REGULATORY AUDIT BASES

A regulatory audit is a planned license or regulation-related activity that includes the
examination and evaluation of primarily non-docketed information. The audit is conducted with
the intent to gain understanding, to verify information, and to identify information that will require
docketing to support the basis of a licensing or regulatory decision. Performing a regulatory
audit is expected to assist the NRC staff in efficiently conducting its review and gaining insights
into the licensee’s processes and procedures. Information that the NRC staff relies upon to
make the safety determination must be submitted on the docket.

The purpose of this audit is for the NRC staff to gain a better understanding of the SPRA report
submitted in response to NTTF Recommendation 2.1, “Seismic,” by providing an opportunity to
review and discuss material used to support analysis and conclusions. The audit is expected to
facilitate a more effective and efficient review by allowing the NRC staff to review and discuss
supporting material with the objective of improving communication and eliminating unnecessary
requests (RAIs) for additional information. The NRC staff plans to audit internal documents,
implementing procedures, and other information needed to verify information and conclusions in
the report. If the NRC staff identifies information that is needed to complete its review, Holtec
Palisades will need to submit that information on the docket.

3.0    SCOPE

Along with appropriate discussion, the audit team will review any documents that provide
technical support for the application.




                                                                                           Enclosure
                                               -2-


4.0   INFORMATION AND OTHER MATERIAL NECESSARY FOR THE REGULATORY
      AUDIT

The NRC staff has identified the following documents it would like to discuss with Holtec
Palisades:

       1. PLP-RPT-16-00001 Rev 0, Amee Foster Wheeler (2015) Final Seismic Hazard
          Evaluation Report, Palisades Nuclear Plant, South Haven, Michigan, December
          2015

       2. PWROG-25021-P Rev. 0. Peer Review of the Palisades Seismic Probabilistic Risk
          Assessment

       3. 38-9400415-000, Palisades SPRA, Seismic Hazard Analysis Summary, NGA-East
          Sensitivity Study and Peer Review Response Activities

       4. 182-9390811-000, Palisades Nuclear Plant Seismic Probabilistic Risk Assessment:
          Model Development Notebook

       5. 38-9297713-000, Palisades Component Fragility Notebook

       6. 51-9392617-000, Palisades SPRA- Fragility Notebook

       7. 38-9297644-002, Palisades Nuclear Plant Seismic Probabilistic Risk Assessment:
          Structural Fragility Analysis

       8. 38-9297605-002, Palisades Nuclear Plant Seismic Probabilistic Risk Assessment:
          Secondary Seismic Hazards

       9. 51-9290041-001, Palisades SPRA - NSSS Fragility Development

       10. 38-9296570-000, Palisades Relay Chatter Analysis Report

       11. 38-9294878-000, Palisades Nuclear Plant Seismic Probabilistic Risk Assessment:
           Structural Response Analysis

       12. 182-9390810-000, Palisades Nuclear Plant Seismic Probabilistic Risk Assessment:
           HRA Notebook

       13. 182-9390809-001, Palisades Nuclear Plant Seismic Probabilistic Risk Assessment:
           Quantification Notebook

The NRC staff may request additional documents or ask questions during the audit.

The NRC staff acknowledges and will observe appropriate handling and protection of
proprietary information made available for the audit. The NRC staff will not remove non-
docketed information from the audit site or web portal.
                                               -3-


5.0    AUDIT TEAM

The audit will be conducted by NRC staff from NRR Division of Risk Assessment and Safety
Systems (DRSS) and the Office of Nuclear Regulatory Research (RES), Division of Systems
Analysis (DSA). The audit will be led by staff from the NRR Division of Licensing Projects 1
(DLP1). Additional audit team members may be added as needed and others may participate as
observers.

Justin Poole, Senior Project Manager, NRR/DLP1
Operating Reactor Licensing Branch 3 (ORLB3)

6.0    LOGISTICS

The audit will be conducted remotely using video and teleconferencing and a secure, online
portal, established by the licensee. The NRC staff requests that all the documents in the audit
scope be provided by Holtec Palisades on an online reference portal. An online reference portal,
established by Holtec Palisades, would allow the NRC staff access to the technical information.
Use of the online reference portal is acceptable provided that Holtec Palisades establishes
measures to limit access to specific NRC staff (e.g., based on NRC e-mail addresses or the use
of passwords which will only be assigned to the NRC staff directly involved in the audit on a
need-to-know basis) and to make the documents view-only (i.e., prevent NRC staff from saving,
copying, downloading, or printing any documents). The conditions associated with the online
reference portal must be maintained throughout the audit process. The NRC staff who should
initially be granted access to the portal are listed in section 5.0. The NRC project managers for
the audit will provide Holtec Palisades with the names of additional NRC staff who should be
granted access. The audit will begin upon issuance of the plan. The NRC staff requests the
portal remain open and accessible until the NRC staff’s safety evaluation report is issued. The
NRC will establish audit meeting(s) on mutually agreeable dates and times to discuss
information needs and questions arising from the NRC’s review of the audited items. The NRC’s
licensing project manager will inform the licensee of audit meeting dates when they are
established, including the date of an audit kickoff meeting.
                                               -4-


7.0    DELIVERABLES

The NRC staff will issue an audit summary report within 90 days of the audit exit. Any audit
summary will be declared and entered as an official agency record and be made publicly
available for viewing through ADAMS.
